records.body: MHRD's Innovation Cell - Online Session Upcoming periodic workshops/ seminars/ interactions with entrepreneurs, investors, professionals MHRD has established ‘MHRD’s Innovation Cell (MIC)’ to systematically foster the culture of Innovation amongst all Higher Education Institutions (HEIs). MIC has envisioned formation of ‘Institution’s Innovation Council (IICs)’ across selected HEIs to conduct various innovation and entrepreneurship-related activities viz. periodic workshops/ seminars/ interactions with entrepreneurs, investors, professionals and has created a mentor pool for student innovators. In order to promote continuous learning and benefit the students, faculties during lockdown period, MIC is providing exclusive opportunity to students and faculty to nurture and prototype new ideas through e-sessions on various innovation / IPR /Start-up related initiatives. Out of planned 17 sessions, 9 online sessions are already completed during 28th April - 8th May 2020 with overwhelming response from faculties, staff and students in terms of number of views and submission of e-assignments. The remaining 8 online sessions will be telecasted on MIC Youtube Channel ( https://www.youtube.com/mhrdinnovationcell ) at 3.00 PM daily from 12th May (Tuesday) till 22nd May 2020 whose details are attached as Annex-1. Past e-session videos are also available on the above link. The basic information’s regarding e-sessions and participation guidelines are as follows. No Prior Registration is required to attend the e-sessions and you can use your smartphone and laptop/desktop. The time slot for the e-sessions are 3.00 PM to 4.00 PM (except Saturday and Sunday) from 12 th May 2020 onwards. Enrollment is Free. No Maximum limit set for Participants, anybody can join the session on YouTube. Faculties, Students, and non-teaching staff can join the e-sessions. Link for the e-Assignment will be available in the e-session page/description box and on submission of the same within 4 working days from the conduct of the e-session. The e-assessment link will be activated after the session is over. Before that e-assessment will not be accessible. In view of the above, you are kindly requested to circulate above information and e-session schedule (Annex-1) among students, faculties, and staff for them to participate and get benefit out of it. For further details, please visit MIC web page at https://mic.gov.in/iicwebinar.php . MHRD-Annex-1_Schedule of IIC e-Sessions - 12th - 22nd May 2020

records.title: Newton Bhabha Fund - Researcher Link Workshop 2020
records.body: Newton Bhabha Fund Researcher Link Workshop Grant 2020 Funding opportunity for leading researchers in I ndia and the UK British Council through Newton Bhabha Fund in collaboration with Department of Biotechnology (DBT) announces Researcher Links Workshop Grant 2020 which is designed to promote international development- relevant research and professional development of early career researchers. The programme gives financial support to bring together a UK and India cohort of early career researchers in a workshop with a potential for long term sustainability. Who can apply for Workshop Grant? Not for profit higher education institutions or publicly funded research organisations that have Leading or Established Researchers are eligible to apply as Lead institutions. Leading or Established Researchers from above mentioned category of institutions can apply to be Principal Applicants (as defined by the European commission - download information here ). Each proposal must have one Principal Applicant from the UK, and one from India. Please click here for full details. Priority areas Applications are invited in the following priority areas: A. Agriculture and allied areas B. Environment and Circular Bio-economy C. Biotechnology-education: research/policy for accelerated development of the sector D. Health E. Artificial Intelligence and Machine learning in Focus areas for each of the above category is available here Support for finding the UK partner University UK International (UUKi) offers a partner matching service to help connect Newton partner country researchers to potential UK partners for Researcher Link workshop Grant call. Those who would like assistance with finding a UK partner can complete UUKi’s Partner Request Form on the UUKi website, before 11 May 2020 . UUKi is then able to suggest UK researchers or research groups which have similar research interests and expertise. Please visit here for full call details
